sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 1$ and $x = 5$. Factoring $(x - 1)(x - 5) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 1$ and $x = 5$.
questions.explanation: Factoring $(x - 1)(x - 5) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 1$ and $x = 5$.

questions.q: A data set recorded for review: equations of lines consists of the four values $\{15, 19, 23, 29\}$. What is the arithmetic mean? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $21.5$. The sum is $15 + 19 + 23 + 29 = 86$, and dividing by $4$ gives $21.5$.
questions.explanation: The sum is $15 + 19 + 23 + 29 = 86$, and dividing by $4$ gives $21.5$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 6x + 3$ in review: equations of lines, evaluate $f(3)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $21$. Substitute $x = 3$: $f(3) = 6(3) + 3 = 21$.

questions.q: Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 2$ and $x = 6$. Factoring $(x - 2)(x - 6) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 2$ and $x = 6$.
questions.explanation: Factoring $(x - 2)(x - 6) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 2$ and $x = 6$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 6x + 3$ in review: equations of lines, evaluate $f(4)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $27$. Substitute $x = 4$: $f(4) = 6(4) + 3 = 27$.

questions.q: Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 3$ and $x = 7$. Factoring $(x - 3)(x - 7) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 3$ and $x = 7$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 6x + 3$ in review: equations of lines, evaluate $f(5)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $33$. Substitute $x = 5$: $f(5) = 6(5) + 3 = 33$.

questions.q: In $\Delta  ABC$ studying equations of parallel and perpendicular lines, $m\angle A = 45^\circ$ and $m\angle B = 45^\circ$. What is $m\angle C$? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.target: Equations of parallel and perpendicular lines
questions.answer: Final Answer: $90^\circ$. Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (45^\circ + 45^\circ) = 90^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (45^\circ + 45^\circ) = 90^\circ$.

questions.q: A geometric figure scaled by factor $k = 2$ has an original side length of $4\mathrm{\ cm}$. What is the corresponding image length? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.target: Equations of parallel and perpendicular lines
questions.answer: Final Answer: $8\mathrm{\ cm}$. Multiplying the original length by the scale factor gives $4 \times 2 = 8\mathrm{\ cm}$.
questions.explanation: Multiplying the original length by the scale factor gives $4 \times 2 = 8\mathrm{\ cm}$.

questions.q: On the coordinate plane, a line with slope $m = 5$ passes through $(0, 4)$. What is its $y$-coordinate when $x = 1$? Show your complete algebraic work.

questions.answer: Final Answer: $9$. Substituting $x = 1$ into $y = 5x + 4$ gives $y = 5(1) + 4 = 9$.
